notes.meaning: God's people sing of a city made strong not by stone walls, but by God's promise to save them. The Lord Himself acts as their shield and fortress against every foe. Believers can rest peacefully because God's protection never fails.

A call goes out to open the city gates so the nation that stays true to God can enter. This points historically to the faithful remnant returning from exile, and spiritually to everyone who trusts in the Lord. Only those who walk in God's truth are welcomed into His holy dwelling.

The Lord promises complete and steady peace to anyone whose mind leans firmly on Him. In Hebrew, repeating the word for peace means a deep and perfect peace that guards the heart in every trouble. When we put our full trust in God, He keeps our thoughts calm and secure.

People are urged to place their confidence in the Lord forever, through every storm and trial. The Lord is called the everlasting Rock, a foundation that will never crack or crumble. Leaning on Him gives believers strength that will carry them into eternity.

God tears down proud rulers and flattens their towering, self-reliant cities into the dust. Then He turns things around by letting the poor and oppressed trample over the rubble. No human strength can stand against the Lord when He rises to defend the humble.

God makes the road of the righteous smooth and level before them. Even when life seems full of rough and steep paths, the upright God guides their steps to a safe finish. He removes hidden traps so His people can keep walking faithfully with Him.

Faithful believers wait patiently for God, even when walking down the hard road of His judgments and discipline. Their deepest inner desire is to honor His name and remember His character. Trusting God in dark times proves that our faith is real.

The prophet yearns for God through the dark night of trouble and seeks Him eagerly as soon as dawn breaks. When the Lord sends His judgments upon the earth, people are shaken out of their carelessness to learn righteousness. Hard times are designed to wake people up and turn them toward the living God.

Wicked people often receive kindness and mercy from God, yet they stubbornly refuse to turn away from sin. Even when living in a land where God's truth is known, they continue to do evil and ignore His greatness. Because they treat God's patience with contempt, judgment must finally fall upon them.

God raises His hand in warning, but stubborn sinners refuse to notice. In the end, they will be forced to see how fiercely the Lord loves and defends His people, and they will be filled with shame. The fire of judgment reserved for God's enemies will completely overtake them.

The Lord will establish lasting peace and blessing for His faithful people. Every good thing they have ever accomplished was actually worked out by God's power and grace. Believers can rest peacefully knowing that God will finish the good work He began for them.

In past days, foreign tyrants and false gods ruled harshly over Israel. But now the people turn away from their old masters to worship and confess the name of the Lord alone. Hard seasons of suffering help believers see their need to serve God with an undivided heart.

The cruel oppressors who lorded over God's people are dead and will never rise again to do harm. The Lord has visited them in judgment, wiping out their power and their memory forever. Every earthly empire that fights against God will eventually sink into ruin.

The Lord has greatly multiplied His people and extended the borders of their land. This expansion brings honor to God, pointing to the gathering of many nations into His kingdom. When God grows His church, His glory shines brightly across the earth.

When painful discipline came upon them, God's people sought Him in distress and poured out quiet, whispered prayers. Their deep sorrow took away pride and brought them into sincere, humble communion with the Lord. Trials often teach us to pray from the heart instead of just with our lips.

God's people felt like a woman in labor, groaning with intense pain and hoping for relief. Yet all their human struggles ended in disappointment, as if giving birth only to wind, without winning freedom or overthrowing their enemies. This showed them that human strength cannot bring salvation; only God can rescue His people.

God answers the cries of His people with a promise that the dead will live and rise again. Just as morning dew refreshes dry ground and brings green plants back to life, God's power will awaken those sleeping in the dust. This promises a joyful resurrection for all who belong to the Lord, rooted in the victory of Christ.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars debate whether this verse speaks of a literal physical resurrection from the grave or uses resurrection as a poetic image for Israel being restored from captivity.

notes.meaning: The Lord invites His people to go into their private rooms and shut the doors, just like the Israelites did during the first Passover in Egypt. They are called to take refuge in prayer and wait quietly while God's anger sweeps away evil. The storm of judgment will last only a little moment compared to the eternal safety God provides.

differ.view: Some understand this verse as a reference to the rapture, where believers are taken to safety in heaven before God pours out wrath during the Great Tribulation.

notes.meaning: The Lord comes out from His heavenly dwelling to punish the people of the earth for their wickedness. The ground will no longer hide innocent blood that was shed, for every hidden evil and murder will be brought into the open. God's righteous judgment guarantees that no wrong done against His people is ever forgotten.
